subject: Agriculture
title: India's Wheat Revolution
description: A short lesson to help you apply India's Wheat Revolution.

hook.text: In 1965, India was one bad monsoon away from mass famine. It imported 10 million tons of wheat per year.

buildup.text: India's agriculture minister, M.S. Swaminathan, brought Borlaug's dwarf wheat seeds from Mexico.

discovery.text: With new seeds, fertilizer, and irrigation, Indian wheat yields doubled in five years.

twist.text: By 1974, India was self-sufficient in wheat. It went from aid recipient to grain exporter.

climax.text: The transformation saved millions from famine but concentrated benefits in Punjab and Haryana—not everywhere.

punchline.text: New seeds turned a hungry nation into a wheat exporter in a decade.

quiz.question: Who brought Borlaug's wheat seeds to India?
